title: File:Caravansary Courtyard Meybod.jpg
why: Working Silk Road caravanserai courtyard (Meybod, Iran) — the fully-rooted end of the permanence ladder's service economy: stables, guest cells, and storage arranged around one shared apron. Anchors the guest-family/service-belt claim with a real staffed inn.

title: File:Hollenberg Pony Express Station NRHP 66000352.jpg
artist: Historic American Buildings Survey (Library of Congress)
why: Surviving 1860 Pony Express HOME station (lodging + spare stock, not just a horse-change) — direct real-world evidence for the rung-2 'family takes root' standing-shed claim.

title: File:RUBY VALLEY PONY EXPRESS STATION.jpg
why: Second surviving station (Nevada, built 1860) — one of only 43 built / 2 that survive; supports the rarity-of-the-rooted-rung claim (most road service never promotes past rung 1 and doesn't survive).

title: File:Ruins of Limekiln House - geograph.org.uk - 862563.jpg
why: A Scottish drove-road staging point ('cattle were rested for a day or two') now a ruin — real-world proof of the degradation-chain property: a rooted waystation reverting to traces banks toward Site 3, exactly as the ladder claims.

title: File:1st Cavalry tent encampment showing the mule shed, Fort Lawton, Washington, July 28, 1900 (KIEHL 283).jpeg
credit: H. Ambrose Kiehl Photograph Collection, University of Washington
why: 1900 cavalry bell-tent camp with mule shed and carrier/store edge visible together — direct evidence for the tent-kit's proposed first-build (bell/cone, one arrayed mesh) plus the store/carrier zone the spec requires beside it.

title: File:Cavalry camp at Fort Lawton, Washington, July 28, 1900 (KIEHL 192).jpeg
credit: H. Ambrose Kiehl Photograph Collection, University of Washington
why: Ordered bell-tent rows with picketed horses and a route tangent along the camp face — evidence for the 'military: ordered rows, tent hierarchy' composition profile already in the catalog, and for the standardized-unit compatibility weight on the bell/cone form.

title: File:Encampment of Beduins..jpg
artist: Boston Public Library / William Vaughn Tupper Scrapbook Collection

title: File:Zaatari Refugee Camp, Jordan by Planet Labs.jpg
why: Satellite view of a real urban-scale hosted/guest camp (~80,000 residents on a bounded site) — the clearest available real-world referent for the guest-family mechanism's urban 'shanty quarter' expression and its loosened population cap.

title: File:Zaatari Refugee Camp John Green 09.png
why: A shop row ('Sham Elysees') selling goods inside the same camp — ground-level proof that an unplanned hosted camp can grow a real service economy (shops, trade, rented goods) without becoming architecture, evidencing the rung-2 'family takes root' claim in an urban-hosted register.
